name: Glycine
note: The smallest amino acid, and the only achiral one — its alpha carbon carries two hydrogens. Its tiny side chain gives backbones unusual flexibility.

name: Alanine
note: A simple methyl group — the reference point for a small hydrophobic side chain.

name: Valine
note: Branched at the beta carbon. Branched hydrophobics cluster in protein cores.

name: Leucine
note: Branched and strongly hydrophobic; very common in membrane-spanning helices.

name: Isoleucine
note: One of two amino acids with a second stereocenter in the side chain (threonine is the other).

name: Methionine
note: Contains sulfur as a thioether. Always the first amino acid of a new protein — AUG is the start codon.

name: Proline
note: Its side chain loops back to the backbone nitrogen, making it a secondary amine. That ring locks rotation, so proline kinks helices and breaks sheets.

name: Phenylalanine
note: Aromatic and hydrophobic — a plain benzene ring with no polar group on it.

name: Tryptophan
note: The largest amino acid. Its indole ring dominates a protein's UV absorbance at 280 nm, which is how protein concentration is measured.

name: Serine
note: A small hydroxyl. Serine is a common active-site nucleophile and a frequent phosphorylation site.

name: Threonine
note: A hydroxyl on a secondary carbon; like isoleucine it has a second stereocenter. Also phosphorylated.

name: Cysteine
note: Two cysteines oxidize to form a disulfide bridge — the only covalent crosslink in tertiary structure. Its thiol pKa of ~8.3 is low enough to be partly deprotonated and highly nucleophilic.

name: Tyrosine
note: Aromatic AND polar, because of the ring hydroxyl. Also a phosphorylation site, and contributes to absorbance at 280 nm.

name: Asparagine
note: The amide of aspartate. Amides are neutral — do not confuse it with the acidic form. Common N-linked glycosylation site.

name: Glutamine
note: The amide of glutamate, and likewise neutral.

name: Aspartate
note: Carboxylate side chain, pKa ~3.9 — well below physiological pH, so it is deprotonated and negative in the body.

name: Glutamate
note: One carbon longer than aspartate, otherwise the same story: negative at physiological pH.

name: Lysine
note: A long flexible chain ending in a primary amine, pKa ~10.5 — protonated and positive at physiological pH.

name: Arginine
note: The most basic side chain, pKa ~12.5. Its guanidinium group is resonance-stabilized, so it stays positive under essentially all physiological conditions.

name: Histidine
note: The one to know cold: pKa ~6.0 sits near physiological pH, so histidine can gain or lose a proton under normal conditions. That makes it the workhorse of enzyme active sites and the only side chain that buffers well at pH 7.
